title: Trump Threatens 25% Tariffs on Canada Over Fentanyl Claims — Canada Exports Almost No Fentanyl
description_short: Trump Threatens 25% Tariffs on Canada Over Fentanyl Claims — Canada Exports Almost No Fentanyl
description_medium: On January 20, 2025, Trump threatened to impose 25% tariffs on Canada, citing fentanyl trafficking as justification despite the fact that Canada accounts for less than 1% of fentanyl seizures at the US border. The vast majority of fentanyl enters the US from Mexico or is produced domestically. Canadian officials expressed bewilderment at the factually unsupported rationale. The threats damaged the longstanding US-Canada relationship and were widely seen as a pretext for broader economic coercion.
description_long: On January 20, 2025, Trump threatened 25% tariffs on Canada and invoked fentanyl trafficking as a justification. Reuters described the announcement as a prospective move, with Trump saying duties on Canada and Mexico could begin February 1 rather than imposing them that first day. The supplied synopsis notes that Canada accounted for less than 1% of fentanyl seizures at the U.S. border, creating a mismatch between the scale of the stated problem and the threatened trade measure. That seizure share is not a complete measurement of every route by which fentanyl reaches users, so the explanation retains its border context. Canadian officials objected to the rationale, and the threats strained relations with a major trading partner. The supported event records the tariff threat and the dispute over its justification. It does not treat January 20 as a completed imposition or establish that the prospective rate remained unchanged throughout later negotiations.
